issues.display_title: Issue #1689: Fix Responsive Header on Mobile
issues.main_description_html:
The mobile header dropdown menu is broken and visually glitches on small screens.

Issues:

  1. The .nav-mobile-menu expands within the document flow and pushes the content below it down, instead of overlaying it.
  2. The .nav-mobile-menu background and backdrop-filter stack on top of the parent .nav's background, resulting in a double-blur effect that looks bad.

Proposed Fixes:

  • Change .nav-mobile-menu to use position: absolute; top: 100%; left: 0; right: 0; width: 100%; z-index: 10; so it overlays content correctly.
  • Add a box-shadow for depth.
  • Fix the backdrop-filter and padding so it renders cleanly and aligns properly on mobile.

Create Exhibition Component Optimization Design

Goal

Deconstruct create-exhibition.component.ts (597 lines) by extracting the complex sequential upload data manipulation logic and the 3D rendering computation (BabylonJS) into a dedicated service. The goal is to make the main component cleaner, focusing solely on managing the UI wizard state.

Architecture

Parent Component:

  • CreateExhibitionComponent: Focuses on managing the wizard flow (Select, Name, Add, Preview), toggling the loading spinner visibility, and navigating the UI.

New Service:

  • ExhibitionUploaderService:
    • Takes over the recursive iteration process for uploading artworks (_runRequestsSequentially, _uploadArtworkImageObject).
    • Constructs the 3D/image payload data before submission (_createUploadPayload, _setInitialPosition).
    • Dynamically loads BABYLON.js and extracts the 3D mesh object dimensions (.glb) using a hidden canvas (_getArtworkObjectScaling).

Data Flow

  • When the user clicks the create confirmation, the component still calls createExhibitionUser to get the exhibition ID.
  • Once the ID is retrieved, the component delegates the execution of the artworkData array upload to ExhibitionUploaderService.processArtworksUpload(...).
  • The service manages the entire upload sequence (including auth checks & error alerts) and returns a result (Promise).
  • The component listens for the Promise result. If successful -> moves to the Preview state; if failed -> displays an error and restores the state.

Verification

  1. The combined upload process for 2D images and 3D models succeeds and they are saved in their original order.
  2. The 3D model (.glb) scaling dimensions can still be extracted accurately.
  3. The scroll reveal animation transitions and the Back/Next buttons in the wizard operate normally.
  4. There are no 3D canvas memory leaks (the engine & scene are successfully disposed of in the service).
